titleEn: While You Wait, Count the Raindrops!

pages.text: "When will the rain stop? I want to see the ducks!" Dingding looked out from the doorway. Dingding had put on the bamboo hat early to play with the ducks below. But rain poured down, and puddles kept growing in the yard.

Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, got the water jug ready. "We'll go when it stops. The banks are slippery now." "I'm bored! I want to go now!" Dingding stamped their feet. Water streamed from the eaves.
Dingding plopped down in the doorway and pouted. "Still raining? Still?" Dingding rested their chin on the threshold. Drops bounced on the big wooden tub in the yard.
Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, sat beside Dingding. "Shall we count raindrops? While You Wait, Count the Raindrops!" "How do we do that?" Dingding tilted their head.
Grandma pointed to the edge of the eaves. Drip, drip, drip. "Count those drops. One, two, three..." She folded her fingers one at a time. Dingding followed. "Four, five, six!"
"After ten, it's your turn." Grandma smiled. "One, two..." Dingding counted. But the drops were coming more slowly now. "Grandma, they're slowing down!"

"When the rain gets weaker, the drops slow down," Grandma whispered. "While You Wait, Count the Raindrops!" Dingding folded their fingers. "One... two...... three........." The gaps between drops grew longer.
Drip... and, much later, drip. Dingding sniffed as wet-soil smells swept into the doorway. "Grandma, the rain stopped!" Dingding jumped up from the threshold.

Now Dingding knew how to wait. "One, count the drops at the eaves! Two, take turns after ten! Three, when they slow down, the rain is ending!" Mom stepped out with the jug and smiled. "You were the first to notice it stopped."

Mom hugged Dingding and straightened the bamboo hat. "Let's see the ducks now!" Counting helped the waiting time pass quickly. Dingding went into the yard, calling, "While You Wait, Count the Raindrops!"
